Every large gas turbine maker in world is booked out for years, because AI data centres need power faster than grids can supply. 

GE Vernova alone has more than 100 gigawatts of gas orders waiting, Bottleneck is not turbine assembly itself, it is castings, means parts made by pouring molten metal into moulds, that go inside them. Indo-MIM grows that casting line near 50% a year. 

Anyone buying this IPO owns small piece of that power shortage

Defence gives Indo-MIM 18.7% of revenue, but much of it means firing mechanism parts for American gun makers, not missiles That market has not grown since 2020, and dealer shelves across United States stay full. 

Gross margin, which is money left after paying for raw material, fell from 86% to 79% last year partly because this defence share shrank. Highest earning corner of business rides on American shoppers, and few people pricing this IPO have noticed

Quietly, Indo-MIM built second business at home. Its metal powder, tooling and traded goods sales jumped from 94 crore rupees in FY24 to 665 crore in FY26, almost entirely inside India, lifting that share of revenue from 3% to 16%. 

Powder earns thinner margin than finished parts, which explains part of last year profit dip. Selling powder locally also puts it inside India young 3D printing supply chain

India has achieved a major milestone in power transmission technology with the successful design, manufacturing and commissioning of its first indigenous 1200 kV Ultra High Voltage (UHV) AC transformer. Developed by BHEL through in-house research and development, the transformer has been installed and commissioned at Power Grid Corporation's 1200 kV National Test Station in Bina, Madhya Pradesh.

The transformer has now been successfully integrated into the power grid, proving its performance under real operating conditions. The transition from laboratory development to field deployment marks a significant technological leap.

Ultra-high voltage transmission is one of the most demanding areas of electrical engineering. While generating electricity has become increasingly efficient with modern technologies, transmitting massive amounts of power across thousands of kilometres with minimal losses remains a far greater challenge. This is precisely where ultra-high voltage transformers play a critical role.

The importance of this breakthrough is particularly significant as India rapidly expands its renewable energy capacity. Large solar parks in Rajasthan and Gujarat, wind projects along the southern coastline, hydropower plants in the Himalayas and future nuclear facilities are often located far from major cities such as Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad. 

With this successful commissioning, India joins an exclusive group of nations like China that have demonstrated advanced capabilities in 1200 kV ultra-high voltage transmission technology. Even USA has 700-800 KV transformer

• 🏛️ The Mumbai City Civil Court has quashed and set aside the order passed by the Estate Officer, Mumbai Port Trust (MBPT)

• 🔄 The Court has remanded the matter back to the Estate Officer for fresh consideration and adjudication on merits after giving all parties an opportunity to be heard

• 📋 The earlier Estate Officer proceedings will now be reconsidered afresh in accordance with applicable law

• 📢 IVP said it will inform the exchanges of any further material developments in the matter

🟢 Impact: Positive (The adverse Estate Officer order has been set aside, providing IVP with another opportunity for a fresh hearing and determination.)

Aurobindo Pharma signs a global licensing agreement with MSD for an investigational HIV prevention medicine.

Aurobindo Pharma has entered into a non-exclusive, royalty-free voluntary licensing agreement with MSD (Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, N.J., USA) for alimatravir, an investigational medicine for HIV prevention.

 - Aurobindo is among a select group of global generic manufacturers chosen to manufacture and supply generic alimatravir.
 - The agreement covers 129 low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), which account for the majority of new HIV diagnoses globally.
 - Notably, the licensing agreements have been executed before the completion of Phase 3 clinical trials, a first in HIV prevention. This is intended to enable faster manufacturing scale-up if the medicine receives regulatory approval.

While commercialization remains subject to successful clinical development and regulatory approvals, the agreement reinforces Aurobindo Pharma's position as a trusted global partner for expanding access to affordable medicines.

For investors, the announcement is strategically important as it strengthens the company's presence in the global access and infectious disease space, while also highlighting its manufacturing and regulatory capabilities.

Ice Make Refrigeration announces a strategic partnership with Japan's Galilei to fuel its next phase of growth.

Ice Make Refrigeration has signed definitive agreements with Galilei Holdings Co. Ltd., a company listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, covering a strategic investment, shareholder partnership, and a manufacturing joint venture.

Here's what stood out 
 
₹190 Cr fund raise
 - ₹180 Cr to be invested by Galilei through a preferential issue of equity shares.
 - An additional ₹10 Cr will be raised from other investors.

Joint Venture with Galilei
A new JV will be established with:
 - Galilei: 60% stake
 - Ice Make Refrigeration: 40% stake
The JV will focus on manufacturing and marketing commercial upright refrigerators, commercial table refrigerators, and related refrigeration products.

 Strengthening growth capabilities
The fresh capital will be used for:
 - Capacity expansion
 - Modernisation of existing facilities
 - Scaling integrated refrigeration and cold-room solutions

Investment in the JV
 - Setting up a new corporate office, Centre of Excellence, and advanced R&D/testing laboratory
 - Repayment/prepayment of existing borrowings to strengthen the balance sheet

Strategic optionality
The company also plans to evaluate select acquisitions in the refrigeration, cold-chain, and allied sectors to expand its market presence and technology capabilities.

This is more than a capital raise. The combination of strategic capital from a global refrigeration player, a manufacturing JV, and a clear roadmap for capacity expansion, R&D, debt reduction, and potential acquisitions makes this a noteworthy development.

Laurus Labs | Q1 FY27 Concall Highlights

Financial Performance
- Record revenue of ₹2,226 crore (+29% YoY).
- EBITDA margin expanded to 31.8%.
- PAT stood at ₹368 crore.
- Gross margin remained strong at 62.7%.
- ROCE improved to 19%.

Business Highlights
- CDMO revenue grew 69% YoY.

- Commercial supplies contributed 55% of CDMO revenue.

- Laurus Bio revenue ₹35 crore (+21% YoY).

- Signed ADC partnership with ARIC Therapeutics.

Growth Strategy
- FY27 capex guidance doubled to ₹2,000 crore.
- FY27–FY28 investments to exceed ₹3,000 crore.
- Investing in Peptides, ADCs and Gene Therapy.
- Fermentation facility operational by FY27-end.
- Krka JV oncology facility due early 2027.

Management Commentary
- Strong customer demand driving capacity expansion.
- Customers prefer ready manufacturing capacity.
- Over 90% of CDMO revenue from patented molecules.
- CDMO business remains well diversified.
- Laurus Bio growth expected over 12–18 months.
- ARV share to decline as non-ARV expands.

Impact
- Positive.
- Record operating performance.
- CDMO demand remains robust.
- Capex reflects growth confidence.
- AI and biotech platforms expanding.
- Strong long-term revenue visibility.

Key Takeaway
- Laurus Labs delivered a strong Q1 FY27 with record profitability and accelerating CDMO momentum. Aggressive investments in fermentation, peptides, ADCs and gene therapy, combined with diversified innovator relationships and a target of CDMO contributing over 50% of revenue by FY30, reinforce a strong long-term growth outlook.

Q1 FY27 Company Results Yesterday

~Company controls the entire journey of creating high-speed data connectivity, starting from raw material to delivering high-speed internet
~Revenue grew by 87% YoY to 1,910 cr; EBITDA margins grew from 13% to 20% YoY
~Order book became 1.6x with just one quarter. Order intake at the end of FY26 stood at 7687 cr, while at Q1 stands at 13100 cr

- Target price at **₹1,109**.

- FY27 guidance cut below expectations.
- EBIT margin exceeded estimates.

- Healthy order book supports outlook.
- Leadership concerns partially addressed.

- Reflects Infosys' meritocratic culture.

- Strong margins offset weak growth.
- Stable deal pipeline reassuring.
- Leadership transition viewed favourably.

- Target price set at **₹1,050**.

- AI-driven pricing deflation continues.
- Daimler contract challenges persist.
- EURS contract termination impacted growth.
- Strong deal wins not converting into revenue.

- Margin defence needed through FY27.
- Ashiss Kumar Dash named next CEO.
- Leadership transition over next nine months.
- Smooth succession expected.

**Impact**
- **Negative**.
- Consecutive guidance downgrades.
- Growth outlook weakened materially.
- Revenue conversion remains soft.
- Leadership change viewed positively.

- **JPM downgraded Infosys to Neutral with a target price of ₹1,050 after another sharp revenue miss and a second consecutive cut in FY27 guidance. Weak demand, AI-led pricing pressure and contract-related issues have hurt growth, although the planned CEO transition to Ashiss Kumar Dash is expected to provide leadership continuity.**

- Target price cut to **₹1,110**.

- Infosys lowered FY27 growth guidance.
- Cut larger than market expectations.
- Near-term business outlook remains weak.
- Relative valuations appear inexpensive.

- Ashiss Kumar Dash appointed new CEO.
- Will assume role from **1 April 2027**.

- Lower growth guidance disappoints.
- Target price reduced significantly.
- Weak near-term earnings outlook.

**JSW Energy | Brokerage Update (CLSA)**

**Rating & Target**
- Rating: Hold.
- Target Price: ₹549.

**Q1 Assessment**
- PAT declined 37% YoY.
- Weak quarter despite thermal acquisition.
- Higher funding costs hurt earnings.
- Lower PPA tariffs impacted profitability.
- Weak generation affected merchant business.

**Brokerage View**
- Merchant power exposure reducing.
- Coal asset additions slowing transition.
- Cuts FY27–FY29 EPS by 11–13%.
- Valuation remains expensive.

**Key Takeaway**
- **CLSA maintains a Hold rating on JSW Energy, citing weak earnings, rising leverage costs, tariff pressure, and slower clean-energy transition despite ongoing capacity expansion.**

**JSW Energy | Brokerage Update (Jefferies)**

**Rating & Target**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target Price: ₹720.

**Q1 Assessment**
- EBITDA beat estimates by 7%.
- Higher capacity additions supported earnings.
- EBITDA grew 3% YoY.
- KSK plant shutdown impacted performance.

**Growth Outlook**
- KSK operations have stabilized.
- Added 1.1 GW capacity so far.
- On track for 2.2 GW FY27 target.

**Key Takeaway**
- **Jefferies maintains a Buy rating on JSW Energy, citing strong capacity additions and execution, with temporary operational disruptions already stabilizing and keeping the company on track for its FY27 expansion plans.**

**Nestlé India | Brokerage Update (CLSA)**

**Rating & Target**
- Rating: Outperform.
- Target Price: ₹1,638.

**Q1 Assessment**
- Sales grew 25.4% YoY.
- Revenue beat CLSA and consensus.
- PAT jumped 49% YoY.
- All segments posted double-digit growth.
- EBITDA margin beat expectations.
- Gross profit saw strongest growth since 3QCY16.

**Growth Drivers**
- Volume-led growth.
- Premiumisation accelerated.
- Quick Commerce boosted premium mix.
- Higher ad spends absorbed well.

**Brokerage View**
- Raises FY27–FY29 earnings by 4–7%.

**Key Takeaway**
- **CLSA reiterates an Outperform rating on Nestlé India, driven by broad-based volume growth, accelerating premiumisation, and strong margin expansion, prompting an upgrade to its earnings forecasts.**

**Nestlé India | Brokerage Update (Citi)**

**Rating & Target**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target Price: ₹1,750 (raised).

**Q1 Assessment**
- Third straight beat-and-raise quarter.
- Revenue, EBITDA and PAT grew strongly.
- Broad-based double-digit segment growth.
- Performance driven by volume growth.
- EBITDA margin expanded to 24.2%.

**Growth Drivers**
- Rural distribution expansion.
- Strong e-commerce momentum.
- Faster premiumisation.
- Higher A&P investments.
- Gross margin and operating leverage improved.

**Key Takeaway**
- **Citi reiterates a Buy rating on Nestlé India and raises its target price to ₹1,750, citing broad-based volume-led growth, sustained market share gains, and margin expansion despite significantly higher brand investments.**

**Eternal | Brokerage Update (HSBC)**

**Rating & Target**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target Price: ₹340.

**Q1 Assessment**
- Food Delivery grew strongly.
- Quick Commerce remained robust.
- Margins improved with operating leverage.

**Brokerage View**
- Q1 supports FY27 estimates.
- Competition appears stabilizing.
- Expects sustained earnings growth.
- Sees 15–20% stock CAGR potential.

**Key Takeaway**
- **HSBC maintains a Buy rating on Eternal, citing strong execution across Food Delivery and Quick Commerce, improving profitability, and confidence in long-term compounding as competitive intensity stabilizes.**

**Eternal | Brokerage Update (Nomura)**

**Rating & Target**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target Price: ₹350.

**Q1 Assessment**
- Food Delivery growth accelerated.
- Quick Commerce rebounded strongly.
- Blinkit profitability improved further.

**Management Outlook**
- Raises steady-state EBITDA margin target to 6%.
- Focus on larger stores and warehouses.
- Expanding assortments and efficiency.
- Better working capital management.

**Brokerage View**
- Expects 57–74% NOV growth in FY27–28.
- Forecasts continued EBITDA margin improvement.

**Key Takeaway**
- **Nomura maintains a Buy rating on Eternal, driven by accelerating growth across Food Delivery and Blinkit, with improving profitability supported by operational efficiencies and scale.**

**Eternal | Brokerage Update (Jefferies)**

**Rating & Target**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target Price: ₹415.

**Q1 Assessment**
- Growth remained high quality.
- Food Delivery outperformed expectations.
- Quick Commerce delivered healthy growth.
- Profitability stayed resilient.

**Management Outlook**
- Competition becoming predictable.
- Value-led Food Delivery seen unsustainable.
- Blinkit avoids aggressive discounting.
- Prioritizes profitable long-term growth.

**Key Takeaway**
- **Jefferies reiterates a Buy rating on Eternal, highlighting disciplined execution, resilient profitability, and management's focus on sustainable growth over market-share gains.**

**Eternal | Brokerage Update (CLSA)**

**Rating & Target**
- Rating: High Conviction Outperform.
- Target Price: ₹506.

**Q1 Assessment**
- Strong execution across businesses.
- Quick Commerce growth accelerated.
- Food Delivery growth gained momentum.
- Profitability improved despite competition.
- Blinkit boosted profitability confidence.

**Growth Drivers**
- Zomato posted fastest growth in six quarters.
- Limited impact from no-commission platforms.
- District and Bistro expanded ecosystem.
- New businesses increased engagement.

**Key Takeaway**
- **CLSA reiterates its High Conviction Outperform rating on Eternal, highlighting strong execution, accelerating growth across core businesses, and rising confidence in Blinkit's profitability despite an intensely competitive market.**

**Eternal | Brokerage Update (JPMorgan)**

**Rating & Target**
- Rating: Overweight.
- Target Price: ₹390.

**Q1 Assessment**
- Results were strong and in line.
- Quick Commerce growth accelerated.
- Blinkit customer additions remained robust.
- QC EBITDA turned positive despite competition.
- Food Delivery growth exceeded estimates.

**Management Outlook**
- Competition likely at peak.
- Confident in handling competitive actions.
- Raises long-term EBITDA margin target to 6%.
- Increases capex per store to ₹25 million.

**Key Takeaway**
- **JPMorgan maintains an Overweight rating on Eternal, citing resilient execution across Blinkit and Food Delivery, improving profitability, and higher long-term margin ambitions despite intense competition.**

**United Spirits | Brokerage Update (CLSA)**

**Rating & Target**
- Rating: Hold.
- Target Price: ₹1,285.

**Q1 Assessment**
- Sales grew 6% YoY.
- Revenue was in line.
- Gross margin expanded 212 bps YoY.
- EBITDA margin contracted 30 bps YoY.
- Higher ad spending hurt margins.
- EBITDA missed estimates.

**Brokerage View**
- Margin below CLSA expectations.
- EBITDA below CLSA and consensus.

**Key Takeaway**
- **CLSA maintains a Hold rating on United Spirits as healthy sales growth was offset by elevated advertising spends, leading to weaker-than-expected margins and EBITDA.**

**United Spirits | Brokerage Update (Nomura)**

**Rating & Target**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target Price: ₹1,500.

**Q1 Assessment**
- Sales met estimates.
- EBITDA missed expectations.
- Premium and Popular volumes declined.
- Gross margin contracted sequentially.
- Higher A&P spend hurt profitability.

**Outlook**
- Expects 1H FY27 headwinds.
- Volume and margin pressure to persist.
- 2H FY27 supported by India-UK FTA.
- MML impact to normalize.
- Softer glass prices to aid margins.

**Key Takeaway**
- **Nomura maintains a Buy rating on United Spirits, expecting near-term pressure to ease in the second half of FY27 as cost headwinds moderate and structural tailwinds improve margins and growth.**

**Dr. Reddy's Laboratories | Brokerage Update (Jefferies)**

**Rating & Target**
- Rating: Underperform.
- Target Price: ₹1,040.

**Q1 Assessment**
- Q1 materially missed estimates.
- Margins hurt by weak US business.
- Higher raw material and SG&A costs.
- India, Russia and Europe grew strongly.

**Management Outlook**
- Expects better margins in 2H FY27.
- Semaglutide delays impacted FY27 outlook.
- Abatacept approval expected by Dec-2026.

**Brokerage View**
- Cuts FY27–FY29 estimates.
- Sees risks from slower Sema ramp-up.

**Key Takeaway**
- **Jefferies retains an Underperform rating on Dr. Reddy's, citing weaker-than-expected profitability and delays in key growth drivers, while expecting margin recovery only in the second half of FY27.**

**Dr. Reddy's Laboratories | Brokerage Update (JPMorgan)**

**Rating & Target**
- Rating: Underweight.
- Target Price: ₹1,100.

**Q1 Assessment**
- Adjusted revenue, EBITDA and PAT declined YoY.
- EBITDA margin at 14.3%.
- Higher SG&A and freight costs hurt margins.
- Core profitability remained weak.

**Management Outlook**
- Semaglutide supply expected by Nov-2026.
- Abatacept approval targeted in early 2027.
- Sees 18–19% EBITDA margin by FY28–29.

**Brokerage View**
- Delays could impact earnings.
- Base business valuation remains expensive.

**Key Takeaway**
- **JPMorgan retains an Underweight rating on Dr. Reddy's, citing structurally weak core profitability and rich valuations, while noting that the expected recovery depends heavily on timely execution of the Semaglutide and Abatacept opportunities.**

**Dr. Reddy's Laboratories | Brokerage Update (CLSA)**

**Rating & Target**

- Target Price: ₹1,240.

- Margin missed due to gSema issues.

**Management Outlook**

- Guides double-digit US base business growth.

- Moderates FY27–FY29 margin estimates.

- **CLSA maintains a Hold rating on Dr. Reddy's as temporary gSema-related disruptions weigh on FY27 earnings, while management remains confident of a recovery through stronger US growth and margin normalization.**

**IndusInd Bank | Brokerage Update (JPMorgan)**

**Rating & Target**
- Rating: Underweight.
- Target Price: ₹820 (Raised).

**Q1 Assessment**
- PAT beat estimates.
- Reported NII and PPoP exceeded expectations.
- Core NII broadly in line.
- Core NIM declined 4 bps QoQ.
- Asset quality improved with lower slippages.

**Management Outlook**
- Targets industry-level FY27 loan growth.
- Aims for 1% exit RoA.
- Operating leverage and lower credit costs to drive recovery.

**Brokerage View**
- Stock up 23% in three months.
- Current valuation seen as pricing in recovery.
- Risk-reward viewed as unfavorable.
